title: Epistemic Wikigraph v2 legacy history stress-test
concept: Claims, evidence, and challenged narratives as a force-directed epistemic audit graph with tiers, falsifiers, M-tags, and narrative conflicts.
warning: This is a stronger internal legacy example, not the default public six-domain history case.

hypotheses.title: Jomon-associated male lines may have survived through asymmetric social incorporation
hypotheses.desc: A paternal-lineage signal that is larger than the maternal signal can be audited as possible asymmetric incorporation. It cannot by itself prove conquest or rule.
hypotheses.fc: Reject or weaken if early Kofun elite ancient DNA shows no elevated D-M55, or if the signal is fully explained by later drift and sampling.
hypotheses.oc: Do not read Y-DNA frequency as proof of conquest.

hypotheses.title: Izanami pollution motifs may preserve transformed memory of contact stress
hypotheses.desc: The mythic structure can be tested as a transformed ritual-political memory of disease, boundary, or contact stress. It is not direct historical testimony.
hypotheses.fc: Weaken if the motif is fully explained by broad myth typology without local ritual or transition-period specificity.
hypotheses.oc: Myth is M-tag evidence and cannot directly prove an event.

hypotheses.title: Kegare concepts may have partly epidemiological contact roots
hypotheses.desc: Pollution and corpse-related taboos may be examined beside agricultural settlement, storage, water, and contact contexts. The link remains abductive.
hypotheses.fc: Weaken if kegare concepts are demonstrably later, unrelated to transition-period contact, or fully explained by non-epidemiological ritual chronology.

hypotheses.title: Koropokkuru may encode memory of northern maritime Jomon-related groups
hypotheses.desc: Folklore, northern genetic structure, and Hokkaido archaeology can be audited together, but folklore remains indirect and analogy-like.
hypotheses.fc: Weaken if Koropokkuru distribution and motifs are shown to be late literary construction without regional continuity.

hypotheses.title: Korean C2b lineages may have a West Liao Neolithic background
hypotheses.desc: Deep subclade timing makes a simple recent bridge unlikely, but the broader northeast Asian background remains testable.
hypotheses.fc: Weaken if subclades are shown to be unrelated to any West Liao or northeast Asian Neolithic context.
hypotheses.oc: Do not use this as direct proof of Japanese migration history.

hypotheses.title: West Liao and Japanese formation should not be treated as directly equivalent
hypotheses.desc: Available distinctions between Japanese C lineages, Korean C2b subclades, and Yayoi components make a direct equivalence claim too strong.
hypotheses.fc: Weaken if securely dated ancient DNA creates a direct, specific bridge into Yayoi or Kofun Japan.

hypotheses.title: The Trans-Eurasian language-origin claim faces lineage and linguistic pressure
hypotheses.desc: The old stress-test treats genetic subclade timing and basic vocabulary mismatch as pressure against a simple language-family migration story.
hypotheses.fc: Weaken if robust regular sound correspondences and matching ancient DNA migration routes are established.

hypotheses.title: Ainu may preserve older Jomon-related linguistic substrate signals
hypotheses.desc: Ainu language isolation and Jomon-related ancestry make a substrate hypothesis auditable, not proven.
hypotheses.fc: Weaken if Ainu can be securely derived from a known external language family with matching historical pathway.

hypotheses.title: Incoming O1b2-associated farmers may have spoken an SVO-linked language
hypotheses.desc: This is a linguistic contact hypothesis, not a demonstrated population-language identity.
hypotheses.fc: Weaken if early incoming farmer contexts are shown to preserve SOV linguistic structure or if SVO comparison fails.
hypotheses.oc: Do not equate Y-DNA, grammar, and language identity directly.

hypotheses.title: Yayoi migration may have imposed disease pressure on Jomon-associated groups
hypotheses.desc: Demographic discontinuity, agricultural settlement, and contact conditions make disease pressure a plausible audit target, but direct pathogen evidence is required.
hypotheses.fc: Weaken if ancient pathogen studies and demographic models show no transition-period disease signal.
